author: Ifmyante
text:
fxdaytrader wrote: I agree with
all of above (except the healthy eating part) and believe a significant
percentage of members are at around break even after struggling for at
least 2 years at the (great) expense of other parts of their life. RTM
is a great, generous place, but forums are not an ideal learning
environment. FF has proved that. Everyone is so desperate to finally
crack it that they read every post and end up going down rabbit warren
after rabbit warren having AHA moments week after week, but with little
in real terms to show for it. It is no use being close to cracking the
code. Reading PA should not be subjective. If it is a skill it is a
skill. I would sign up for anything you choose to do out of respect for
your ability, humility and generosity, but hopefully you can address
this basic frustration. Trading is a confidence game - if you don't have
 it with your methodology you end just staying on the "learning
treadmill" - which as fascinating as it is, starts getting a bit old. I
wish you the best with whatever choices you make. FX

I understand exactly where you're coming from

If I do this, it will be a step by step course, undiluted by repetition or contradiction.

The trading methods taught would be absolutely objective, rule based if
you will, although these rules would be meaningless without the ability
to read price in the first place.

So the first part of the course would be all about the read, and later
there'd be the trading module, where there'd be a method and set of
rules for each trading style and trader's lifestyle - as I've never
taught my trading methods before, this is the bit that gets me really
excited :)

author: DharmaTrader
text:
If,

When I first came across the PIE thread, what really grabbed my
attention was one of your videos which had been linked. You have a way
of teaching which really gets the point across and without the arrogance
 and chest thumping which is often the case with people who are very
skilled in their area of expertise whether it be trading, sports,
academia or whatever. You are a gifted teacher and I feel very
fortunate to have landed here at RTM.

A few years ago, I had what I consider an epiphany concerning why people
 do what they do. I'm not really a live music fan but I was at the ski
slope one day and they were having a free concert and you could see that
 tons of people were just totally into the music and really in the zone.
 What makes a person listen to music like that or be a rock climber or
do any specific activity that they have a passion for? I believe that
people are drawn to whatever brings them into the Present Moment the
most. We are meant to BE, actually live, in this moment. For you,
teaching may be one of the things that does this.

Regarding your question about setting up a full blown training program, I
 have no doubt that anything that you put together would be extremely
beneficial to those who study it. My question is, would doing that
really speak to the teacher in you?

For many, myself included, trading is a means to an end, with the end
being any number of things that the person would really like to be
doing. We've all seen the list many times: travel, spending time with
family, not being stuck in the 9 to 5 daily grind, etc.

If you find yourself in the enviable situation where you can relax for a
 bit and not DO anything, perhaps that is a good place to spend a little
 time, take a few breaths and see what comes your way. When we don't
have everything planned and are open to something new it's often amazing
 to see what the Universe delivers...

DT

author: rcmacf
text:
I miss my days of teaching (instructing adults in some oilfiled
operations and data analysis) and take opportunities wherever I can to
pass on my knowledge, so I understand the drive to do so in others. So,
 I say go for it, as it won't leave you, and will burn away until you
find an outlet.

For RTM specifics, I'd like to mirror the thoughts of a few others, that
 I'm off down rabbit holes with walls at the end (PAZ, anyone? I'm
almost embarrassed to ask for direct help with this, so long have I been
 trying to make it work in my head, without subjectivity) and I can feel
 an internal struggle starting, pushing me back to the comfort of old
ways. My desire to master this RTM way is strong, however, and it shall
 win through.

On the other hand, there are so many sheisters in trading that I feel
uncomfortable with the 'cost' option being used to exclude people from
knowledge. I know of "elite" groups charging $25,000 for membership yet
 giving no more knowledge or profit than I've gleaned from a week with
youtube. Also, the people who would like to take your proposed course
are more than likely (like me) those who have struggled to make trading
work for them, even though success is right there - look,
right......there......just out of reach, and so a big financial
commitment has the potential to be yet another market related kick in
the balls. I have been involved in groups, for example, where your
happy, free, trading helper starts pushing more and more products your
way, until you suddenly realise that their methods don't work for them,
either, and the products are their bread and butter (and more often than
 not somebody else's, just repackaged). Yuck.

I've given much time to the markets, and have even been passing on the
knowledge I have to others for concepts that I know inside out so it
would be great if this was my last rabbit hole, and I could stop
chasing, chasing, chasing.

Forums can take you so far, but as this one grows, so do the rabbit
holes. They may lead somewhere good, but how to know when you start at
the top?

My approach, perhaps, has been unfocussed, and this is where a course
would be of the most use to me. I have not completed all the homework,
and so perhaps this is where I am failing, although I think I have a
good enough grasp on the concepts. However, there is a purity to how
you see the markets, IF, and that is diluted (you could say enhanced) by
 all the others teaching on this site. You can't police it all, and so
there chance of the new going down the wrong hole is always there.

Anyhoo, I put together videos as it's always a struggle for me to get my
 point over effectively via a keyboard without about 45mins per
sentence. Ok, about 10 words per minute, but all the same.

author: Ifmyante
text:
Thanks RC

Do get to grips with doing the homework - It's here that the lessons
will become real for you - all the answers are on the charts - this site
 is just a guide to reading them. I've shown you exactly what to look
for, so just have patience with yourself and look.

There's absolutely NO NEED FOR ANYBODY TO PAY FOR A TRADING COURSE,
 run by me or anybody else. Simply watch my videos, read my articles and
 posts, and always ask yourself "What should he have added to that?"
Believe me, what should've been added is on the site, in another video
or post.

I just want to re-do all my lessons, and, being very bad at keeping
secrets, want to share everything I've learned in one course :)
